messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I sketched a short playbook for apples-to-apples benchmarks when we compare kernel choices and batching heuristics across replay vs synthetic traffic. TL;DR: align sample-rate, seed, seq-len distribution, and prefix warmup; measure TTFT/TPOT + p95/p99 + goodput vs QPS. Want quick feedback before I formalize it.

Maria: pls drop the checklist here. The last time we missed aligning sample-rate and the results were noisy.

Alex: Checklist draft below (high level):
- Fix sample-rate and RNG seed for both replay/synth
- Use identical seq-len histogram (bucket by tokens)
- Ensure same prefix / KV-cache warmup strategy (explicit warmup runs)
- Run 3 independent trials, report mean + stdev
- Capture: TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99, goodput (tokens/sec served to model), QPS (requests/sec), KV-hit-rate, GPU util, and memory growth
- Tag kernel/config and model version; no mixing during comparison

Jamal: + add a short command snippet for reproducibility. Example we use locally:
```bash
# replay harness
python harness/replay_run.py --trace ./traces/customerA.json --sample-rate 0.02 --seed 42 --warmup 500 --out run_replay.json
# synth generator (match seq-len histogram)
python harness/synth_gen.py --hist ./traces/hist.json --n-req 200000 --seed 42 --out run_synth.json
```
Make sure batching config file is identical for both runs.

benchbot: run-summary for run_replay.json (2149001290): QPS=185.2, TTFT_p95=210ms, TPOT=18.3 tok/s, goodput=16.1 tok/s, KV_hit=0.62, GPU_util=74%, kernel=fast_attn_v2.

Sree: benchbot numbers look ok but remember: KV_hit skews TPOT->goodput ratio. If synthetic traffic has different prefix locality you can get +10–40% diff. For apples-to-apples we must annotate per-request KV-hit (or at least per-batch). Also capture KV cache size & eviction counts.

Vik: For kernel selection heuristics I'd propose: baseline = current kernel. New kernel should be promoted only if across *representative* seq-len buckets: median(TTFT) <= baseline_TTFT * 1.05 AND avg(TPOT) >= baseline_TPOT * 1.07. Also require no regression in p99 > baseline_p99 * 1.10. These thresholds are tunable but prevent churn.

Maria: +1 to thresholds. Also we should normalize for cost: compute TPOT per GPU-dollar (or per vGPU-minute). Sometimes a kernel gives lower latency but costs more because it disables some batching paths.

Alex: On metrics definitions (short canonical defs we should use in reports):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): wall-clock from request accept -> first model token emitted (ms)
- TPOT (tokens-per-op-time): sustained token throughput measured at model exec (tokens/sec) including kernel-level batching effects
- p95/p99: percentiles on per-request latency (for TTFT and full-response)
- Goodput: tokens/sec that are actually delivered to the model (excluding duplicates/no-op retries); prefer goodput when evaluating per-token cost
- QPS: requests/sec at the API surface (useful for load shaping, but not substitute for token-level metrics)

Jamal: tiny note: when we measure TPOT we must define the measurement window (e.g., exclude initial warmup window W seconds and tail warmdown). Otherwise short runs bias TPOT.

Sree: Another practical gotcha — batch formation heuristics can depend on request concurrency patterns. In synthetic runs we must simulate the same concurrency envelope (burstiness, steady-state) not just mean QPS. Use Poisson bursts or replay arrival times.

benchbot: posted additional meta from profiler (2149001355): kernel fast_attn_v2 shows 12% lower op-time for long-seq bucket (>1024) but 6% worse for short-seq (<128). Batch-size distribution: skewed toward small batches (60% <4) in replay trace.

Vik: That explains why fast_attn_v2 improved TPOT but TTFT p95 regressed on small-reqs. Action: either tune fallback path for small batches or use smart routing: route short-reqs to baseline kernel. We should capture routing rules as part of the bench metadata.

Alex: Action items (quick):
1) Jamal: add sample-rate + seed flags to harness and commit to infra (due EOD)
2) bench infra: emit per-request KV-hit, eviction count, and per-batch size distribution into run JSON (Sree)
3) Vik: codify kernel promotion heuristic as above and add to README
4) Maria: add cost-normalized TPOT computation to report template
5) Everyone: run one apples-to-apples (replay vs synth) with identical configs and paste run JSON here for review

Maria: Sounds good. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to walk through the first run. :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks — I'll update the doc with these edits and ping when the harness PR is ready. :rocket:
